title: Analytics & Reporting on Data Cloud
docTitle: Phase 12: Analytics & Reporting on Data Cloud
html:
Unified data is only valuable when it is seen. This phase covers how Data 360 data reaches Tableau/CRM Analytics, Data 360-specific reporting, dashboards on unified profiles, and KPI design — plus the lab's DataCloudReportingService that builds and reads the CRM-side dashboard/reports shipped with this repo.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Explain how Data 360 DMOs and unified profiles are exposed to Tableau/CRM Analytics.
  • Choose report/dashboard sources (Data 360 data source vs CRM materialized fields) per requirement.
  • Design service/marketing KPIs over unified data (CSAT, churn, LTV, pipeline velocity).
  • Read and extend DataCloudReportingService and the shipped dashboard/reports.

1. Data 360 → analytics platforms

Data 360 integrates with analytics in two broad modes:

ModeHowBest for
Data 360 data source in Tableau/CRM Analytics (live)Query DMOs/unified profiles and insights directlyLive, on-the-fly analytics over unifyed data
Export/materialize to CRM + report on CRMData actions materialize attributes/segments onto Contact/AccountNative reporting UX, Salesforce1, sharing
Marketing Cloud reportingEngagement data stays in MC analytics, or goes to Data 360 for cross-source viewsCampaign analytics

Shared key discipline

Whatever the sink, the key is the same IndividualId/external key. If your dashboards join on different keys per source, reconciliation breaks. Storing sfdc_recordId/external keys at ingestion (Phases 2–3) is what makes cross-system dashboards possible.

2. Reporting on unified profiles: patterns

The canonical service-analytics patterns and their Data 360 shapes:

KPIInsight/SQLWhere visualized
Customer 360 healthCOUNT(UnifiedIndividual), profiles-w/-tid-data %CRM Analytics overview
Churn riskChurn_Score insight ≥ thresholdDrill from segment → individuals
Lifetime valueSUM(Order.totalamount) per IndividualCohort tables
Service backlog by segmentCase DMO joined to Unified profileService dashboard
Marketing attributionEngagement data + order data joinedFunnel reports

Dashboards over unified profiles let you slice a report that the CRM alone cannot (e.g. customers in the "At-Risk" segment with 2+ open cases, where the segment is the Data 360 filter and the cases are the CRM detail).

3. KPI design for service (consultant skill)

A Data 360 consultant is expected to design the KPI set, not just build charts. The reliable starter set:

  1. CSAT / NPS by segment — satisfaction anchored to profile attributes, not just case records.
  2. First-contact resolution (FCR) — needs a case-level resolution metric across sources.
  3. SLA adherence — SLAs on entitlements, verified against the unified contract view.
  4. Churn score trend — the predictive metric as a profile attribute (Phase 13).
  5. LTV/CAC ratio — calculated insight over orders + spend; the north-star commercial KPI.

Design rule: every KPI needs a measure, a dimension, a granularity, and a refresh — the same discipline as Phase 5. Write them down before building.

4. The lab: DataCloudReportingService

apex
public with sharing class DataCloudReportingService {
    public static Map<String, Decimal> kpiSummary(Set<Id> leadsOrProfiles) { ... }
    public static List<Service_KPI__c> recentKpis(String domain, Integer limitRows) { ... }
}

It: (1) computes a small KPI summary from the CRM-side mirrors (KPI_Metric__c, SLA_Compliance__c, Segmentation counts), (2) boundary-guards missing input, and (3) reads back recent Service_KPI__c rows. The repository ships a dashboard (Data_360_Kpis in dashboards/) and two reports (Unified_Profile_Coverage and Segment_Membership) under reports/ so you can open the same story in Lightning — the twin of a Data 360 analytics view.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Dashboard source decision

For each: (a) live churn drill-down for the CSO; (b) a Salesforce1 report "open cases by lifetime value"; (c) marketing newsletter click-through. Choose Data 360 live source vs materialize-to-CRM and justify.

Exercise 2: KPI design

Write the measure/dimension/granularity/refresh table for: "SLA adherence by segment", "LTV by acquisition channel", "churn score trend (weekly)". Note which columns must exist on the unified profile or an insight.

Exercise 3: Lab build

Open DataCloudReportingServiceTest, add a KPI scenario (3 accounts with spend + one with an SLA breach) and assert the summary returns the correct totals and that recentKpis limits to limitRows.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
CRM AnalyticsTableau-powered analytics built on Salesforce data, incl. Data 360 data sources.
Unified-profile reportingDashboards/reports that slice by identity-resolved attributes and segments.
Measure / dimensionThe numeric aggregate and its grouping attribute (revisited from Phase 5).
Materialize-to-CRMPersisting Data 360 attributes onto CRM records for native reporting.
KPI designSpecifying measure, dimension, granularity, refresh before building.
Drill-throughNavigating from an aggregate chart to the underlying member list.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can choose Data 360 live vs CRM materialized reporting per requirement.
  • I can design the core service/marketing KPI set with proper specs.
  • I can build a dashboard that slices Data 360 segments against CRM detail.
  • I can read, extend, and test DataCloudReportingService.

Self-Check

  1. Q: Where do you query unified customer data for analytics? — A: The DMO/UnifiedIndividual via the Data 360 data source in CRM Analytics/Tableau (or materialized CRM fields for native reporting).
  2. Q: Why do dashboards break when keys differ? — A: Every source must share the same IndividualId/external key; sfdc_recordId stored at ingestion keeps joins reliable.
  3. Q: KPI design — measure, dimension, granularity, refresh. Give an example for SLA adherence. — A: measure = % breaches, dimension = segment, granularity = entitlement, refresh = daily (or real-time for live ops).
